newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's Bharat Petroleum plans FCC shutdown in Feb.
newsitem.headline: India's Bharat Petroleum plans FCC shutdown in Feb.

text.p: Indian state refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd plans to shut down a 900,000 tonne a year (18,000 barrel-per-day) fluid catalytic cracker at its Bombay refinery in February for 30 days of maintenance, a company official said on Tuesday.
"The final decision will be made in the middle of January," Director of Finance Ashok Sinha told Reuters.
He said the state Oil Coordination Committee, which oversees India's maintenance schedules, will make the decision.
The FCC's shutdown at BPCL's 120,000-bpd refinery was previously scheduled for November, but has been postponed by a few months.
Sinha said there were no product shortages and the scheduled turnaround of one of the refineries belonging to state refiner Indian Oil Corp Ltd was the cause of the delay.
Sources had told Reuters earlier this month that the IOC had plans to delay the December turnaround of the 50,000-bpd crude distillation unit at its 192,000 bpd Koyali refinery until 1997.
